findings.message:
[P2] Align the run-summary target cap with the raised bound

Raising `TARGETS_MAX` to 64 makes target files with 51-64 entries valid, but `src/host/run-summary.ts:92` still sets `MAX_TARGETS = 50` and line 116 slices each child target list to that length. Any accepted configuration above 50 targets will silently omit later targets and their admitted/skipped counts from the run summary, so the new headroom is not reflected end to end. This does not affect the current 30-target file, but it should be aligned with `TARGETS_MAX` or made an explicit, visible truncation.

src/host/targets.ts:50-50

summary: The change raises TARGETS_MAX from 32 to 64 with a stated one-coordinator and bounded-setup rationale and adds coverage for 33, 64, and 65 target settings. One follow-on bound remains below the new accepted maximum: the advisory run-summary parser still drops targets beyond 50.

evidence: src/host/targets.ts:42-50 raises `TARGETS_MAX` from 32 to 64 and records the one-coordinator, bounded per-target setup and unchanged admission/deadline reasoning requested by the issue.
tests/host/targets_test.ts:167-239 covers ordered parsing at 33 and 64 entries, ordered 64-target loading, and fail-closed rejection of 65 entries before repository reads.
The shipped `sentinel.targets.json` remains 30 entries, so the new bound leaves 34 entries of headroom beyond the current rollout while core target loading accepts the expanded range.
